expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: Four interfaces (TrialingSubscription, ActiveSubscription, PastDueSubscription, CanceledSubscription) each with `readonly status: "trialing"|"active"|"past_due"|"canceled"`, combined in `type Subscription = TrialingSubscription | ActiveSubscription | PastDueSubscription | CanceledSubscription`

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: CanceledSubscription has only {id, customerId, planId, startedAt, status, canceledAt, cancellation}; no trialEndsAt or other variant-specific fields

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: `function assertNever(x: never)` defined; used in switch default case in `billingBannerFor()` function; recommends `@typescript-eslint/switch-exhaustiveness-check`

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: SubscriptionId, CustomerId, PlanId all defined as `Brand<string, ...>`; RetryCount also branded as `Brand<number, ...>`

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Five transition functions (convertTrialToPaid, renew, paymentFailed, paymentRecovered, cancel) constrain transitions by signature; e.g., `renew(canceledSub, …)` doesn't typecheck because no function accepts CanceledSubscription

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Table enumerating misuses before types; then explains each: 'renew(canceledSub, …) don't typecheck', 'Nothing accepts a CanceledSubscription, which makes canceled terminal by construction', 'a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date'

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary recommendation is discriminated union with transition functions; bag-of-optionals is listed as a misuse: 'Flat {...} — 2⁶ spellings for 4 states'
